artists.name: Racionais MC's
artists.sobre: Há 35 anos, Mano Brown, Kl Jay, Ice Blue e Edi Rock colocam em evidência a realidade do jovem preto e periférico no Brasil. A trajetória compartilhada entre o quarteto de maior impacto da música nacional atravessou barreiras além do rap, se tornando pilar de referência na cultura do país. De 1988 pra cá, a história foi contada por meio de rimas e versos que ecoam por gerações, com discos e EPs como Holocausto Urbano (1990), Escolha o seu Caminho (1992), Raio X Brasil (1993), Racionais MC’s (1994), Sobrevivendo no Inferno (1997), Nada Como Um Dia Após O Outro Dia (2002), 1000 trutas, 1000 tretas (2006) e Cores e Valores (2014). Não à toa, o recém-lançado documentário original Netflix “Racionais: das ruas de São Paulo para o Mundo”, que mostra o caminho percorrido pelos artistas por meio de letras de resistência e denúncia, ocupou a sexta posição do TOP 10 Global da plataforma ⎯ como filme em língua não inglesa. Ao longo de 2022, a turnê Racionais MC’s 33 World Tour atravessou cidades pelo Brasil, dominando palcos de importantes festivais nacionais como o CENA 2k22, Forró da Lua Cheia e Rock in Rio. E, no mesmo ano, ainda levaram a turnê para os Estados Unidos, passando por 5 estados ao longo de 13 dias: Nova York, Connecticut, Nova Jersey, Massachusetts e Flórida (Miami e Orlando). Agora, enquanto Mano Brown, Kl Jay, Ice Blue e Edi Rock preparam novos trabalhos em estúdio, o grupo visa ocupar novos palcos e espaços.

artists.name: The Notorious B.I.G.
artists.sobre: In just a few short years, the Notorious B.I.G. went from a Brooklyn street hustler to the savior of East Coast hip-hop to a tragic victim of the culture of violence he depicted so realistically on his records. His all-too-brief odyssey almost immediately took on mythic proportions, especially since his murder followed the shooting of rival  by only six months. In death, the man also known as Biggie Smalls became a symbol of the senseless violence that plagued inner-city America in the waning years of the 20th century. Whether or not his death was really the result of a much-publicized feud between the East and West Coast hip-hop scenes, it did mark the point where both sides stepped back from a rivalry that had gone too far. Hip-hop's self-image would never quite be the same, and neither would public perception. The aura of martyrdom that surrounds the Notorious B.I.G. sometimes threatens to overshadow his musical legacy, which was actually quite significant. Aided by Sean 'Puffy' Combs' radio-friendly sensibility, Biggie reestablished East Coast rap's viability by leading it into the post- gangsta age. Where fellow East Coasters  slowly built an underground following, Biggie crashed onto the charts and became a star right out of the box. In the process, he helped Combs'  label supplant  as the biggest hip-hop imprint in America, and also paved the way to popular success for other East Coast talents like  and . Biggie was a gifted storyteller with a sense of humor and an eye for detail, and his narratives about the often-violent life of the streets were rarely romanticized; instead, they were told with a gritty, objective realism that won him enormous respect and credibility. The general consensus in the rap community was that when his life was cut short, Biggie was just getting started.

artists.sobre: Madvillain is yet another collaboration by Stones Throw big shot , this time with masked MC . , who had been listening to 's Operation: Doomsday (1999), was impressed by the MC's lyrics and beats and contacted  to talk about the possibility of working together. Though  had never heard of  at that point, as soon as he heard the DJ's work he agreed immediately. The two met up in 2002 at the Stones Throw headquarters in Los Angeles and instantly clicked.  introduced Madvillain to the world in 2002 at the Red Bull Music Academy in Brazil, and in 2004 Madvillainy, the completed record, was released, and was one of the more critically acclaimed albums of the year. ~ Marisa Brown, Rovi
